confirmed: The complete markdown and all 9 PDF pages were read. The local PDF is undated, has metadata title "ICoRD Published manuscript", and shows no manuscript date or revision identifier; the title and three authors match the form (p. 1; PDF metadata; pp. 1-9).

The main comparison uses ALIA versus a control allowed internet resources, without stating any allocation mechanism; design_class other and randomized not_stated are supported (p. 6, Section 3.5; full-text review).

The reported group composition is 6 groups per condition, 2 participants per group except one control group with 3, establishing fewer than 50 people; separate randomized and analyzed-person totals are not printed (p. 6, Section 3.5).

Participants were university students aged 18 to 20 and fresher design undergraduates; the same six problem statements were used across conditions in approximately 30-minute sessions (p. 6, Section 3.5; p. 7, Section 5).
ALIA supplies context-dependent words and questions using speech transcription and discussion summaries; the model is Mistral 7b (pp. 4-5, Sections 3.1-3.4 and Figures 1-2; p. 7, Section 5).

The reported string and one-line finding match the plotted Good self-ratings exactly: experimental 9 (75%) and control 5 (38.5%) (p. 7, Figure 4, right-hand panels, inspected directly as an embedded PDF image).

Figure 4 labels both control panels 13 responses, experimental difficulty 12 responses, and experimental idea ratings 13 responses; experimental idea-rating bars are Poor 0, Bad 1, Okay 1, Good 9, Excellent 1. The form accurately flags this inconsistency and leaves the distinct analyzed-person counts null (p. 7, Figure 4).

The reported outcomes are participants' post-session feedback and self-assessments. The paper limits its evaluation to participants' reactions and defers analysis of the produced ideas and their novelty; no qualifying output-scored creativity or diversity outcome or inferential contrast is reported (p. 2, Section 1; pp. 6-7, Section 4 and Figure 4; p. 7, Section 5; p. 8, Section 6).

Three preliminary functionality pilots are mentioned collectively, without pilot-specific participant counts, allocation details, or scored creative-output outcomes (p. 2, Section 1; p. 5, Section 3.3).

Core exclusion and context_class none are supported by the self-report-only evidence; no study reports both random assignment to AI assistance and a qualifying output score (p. 2, Section 1; pp. 5-8, Sections 3.3-6; codebook Section 3).
This is an empirical prototype evaluation, not a synthesis; there are no pooled estimates, and no supplement or appendix is identified in the complete document (pp. 1-9, ending with references).
summary: The form is supported: assignment is unstated, the main sample is below 50, and only self-reported outcomes are reported. Figure 4 confirms the quoted percentages and the experimental response-count inconsistency, so no corrections are needed.
